fixed.how: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts, on the safe side (when unsure, a line is work left). (1) The general rule is now a closed allowlist form, SAYS_ONLY_NOTHING_LEFT. It accepts nothing/none, then LEFT words (else, more, is left, is needed, to do ...), then what the line is about: a preposition and the whole set (for, in, by, against, on, within, to meet, 'listed in' ...) or a relative clause ('[that] the brief lists', 'the criteria have asked for'). After that comes at most one more LEFT word or 'remains', and nothing else. WORK_STATE is removed, and WHOLE_SET, ONE_CRITERION and NOT_NOTHING still apply. (2) ABOUT's middle is a closed list, ABOUT_WORD: the, this, the task's, acceptance, the scope of, each of ... (3) reasonSaysDone: a reason after punctuation, in both NOTHING and RELATIVE_HEAD, counts only when it has a done word (met, covers, written, opened, lists ...). It must name nothing still to come (remain, pending, left, to do, need to, then ...; 'nothing remains' inside the reason is allowed) and no part may start with an order ('write ...'). Every L4-money-101, W15-14 and L3-research-1 case stays green, including the composed LC-C7 live report, the live F4 and L3 reports, and the bench stand-in's FORERUNNER_BENCH_LEFT_NOTE line. The composed case now pauses with exactly '"Write the Swiss pairing rules" paused before its budget of CHF 0.15 ran out: it spent CHF 0.10 and listed one thing left to do; CHF 0.04 is kept for its review.' Its card is '"Write the Swiss pairing rules" paused before its budget ran out' with 'Continue (CHF 0.16 more)' and 'Cancel task', and the task is not reviewed. ADR 0112 has a dated amendment (2026-11-22, l4c-workstate) because the rule's meaning changes. runtime.md and the user guide are updated.

fixed.how: In packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts, reasonSaysDone is now an allowlist. The reason is split at punctuation and 'and'. Each part must match one closed form. IS_DONE: an optional subject, is/are/was/were/has been, then a DONE_STATE word ('both are met', 'notes.md is written', 'each part of it was checked', 'all met', 'complete'). DOES_ALL: a subject that does it to all of it ('hosts.md covers each of them', 'each listed page gives its address', 'the file lists every page it names', 'I checked each one'). ALL_PASS: 'all tests pass', 'the tests pass'. NONE_LEFT: 'nothing remains', 'so nothing is left', 'no work left', 'no further work needed', 'no outstanding items'. A part fails if it holds any of these: a qualifier or hedge (QUALIFIED: partly, mostly, half, N%, some, most, 'two of the three', only, first, draft, main, core, happy, probably, seems, hopefully, I think, so far, and 'part(s)' unless each/every/all stands before it); an exception or condition (apart from, other than, save for, bar, besides, aside, short of, minus, without, once, after, when, if, until, unless, as soon as); a future (to be, will, can, next, later, awaiting, an infinitive 'to add'); work still to come; 'nothing', 'none' or 'nobody' as what is done; an order. Anything else is work. aboutWholeSet still requires isNothing, so a whole-set 'nothing' makes other items notes only when its reason passes this form. fixed.how: SAYS_ONLY_NOTHING_LEFT now has a guard, (?!\s+of\b), so a line that starts 'none of' or 'nothing of' never reads through the general rule. No positive case needs 'None of the criteria need ...', so it was not kept. The rule now reads named groups through saysOnlyNothingLeft. What a line is about says nothing of it is left on its own only in two cases: its verb says what the set needs (NEEDS: require, ask for, call for, want, expect), or its preposition is 'for' or 'to meet'. Two kinds need a LEFT word before or after: a verb that only says what the set holds (HOLDS: lists, names, covers, included, mentions, describes, specifies, sets out), and a place (in, by, under, within, against, on, from, or NAMED_BY + in). The older NOTHING form follows the same rule: a bare 'nothing' or 'none' with 'in', 'by' or 'under' needs a LEFT word. 'within', 'for' and 'to meet' still read as nothing on their own, so W15-14's 'Nothing within the scope of the brief' is unchanged.
